_coverage_rationale: REF-DEAL-6: Deck-only company (no XLSX) with a dense KPI slide and multiple pricing traps. Tests the system's ability to read a KPI-heavy deck without mistaking pricing tiers, license fees, or market-size numbers for company revenue. The existing deck-only deal (Qredible) has only a few key figures; this profile targets a deck with 4+ pricing mentions, a competitor comparison table, and a market size slide all on the same page as the traction KPIs. It also exercises multi-metric traction: DAU, WAU, paid users, MRR, LTV, CAC — verifying the system picks the right fields for each metric_key rather than the highest-value number.
_failure_modes_targeted: Pricing trap: '$99/month per seat' becoming burn_rate or revenue via deck NLP
Market size trap: '$4.2B TAM' promoted to revenue by a deck fact labeler that sees a large dollar figure
Competitor ARR trap: deck says 'Competitor X does $50M ARR' — system assigns that as company ARR
LTV/CAC trap: '$1,200 LTV' vs '$120 CAC' — LTV inflated to MRR or ARR
Multi-currency: deck mixes USD MRR with GBP-denominated enterprise contract values — both must map to the same currency
Wrong MRR selection: deck lists 3 MRR figures (total, recurring, expansion) — system must pick total MRR not the highest

slots.company_description: __FILL IN from deal product profile or pitch deck__

financials._note: Target shape: PDF deck only, no XLSX. Deck must have: (1) a KPI slide with at least 3 traction metrics (e.g. MRR, paid users, ARR), (2) a pricing page with multiple price points, (3) a competitor comparison table with competitor revenue/ARR figures, (4) a market opportunity slide with TAM/SAM/SOM figures. The 'correct' company financials come ONLY from the traction slide — all other figures are noise.
